item.title: Notice of Final Federal Agency Actions on Proposed Highway: Topsham, Maine — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'

item.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.
item.content:encoded: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

item.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Framework Adjustment 7 to the Atlantic Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: NMFS proposes measures included in Framework Adjustment 7 to the Spiny Dogfish Fishery Management Plan (FMP), as recommended by the Mid-Atlantic and New England Fishery Management Councils. Framework 7 proposes fishing year 2026 and projected 2027 specifications, which would establish allowable harvest levels for the spiny dogfish fishery to prevent overfishing while enabling optimum yield based on the best scientific information available. Framework 7 also proposes changes to the Atlantic spiny dogfish accountability measures intended to provide the commercial fishery with greater flexibility by no longer requiring full payback of annual catch limit (ACL) overages when the Atlantic spiny dogfish stock is considered healthy.

item.title: Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act Provisions; Atlantic Coastal Fisheries Cooperative Management Act Provisions; General Provisions for Domestic Fisheries; Application for Exempted Fishing Permits — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Assistant Regional Administrator for Sustainable Fisheries, Greater Atlantic Region (GARFO), NMFS, has made a preliminary determination that an Exempted Fishing Permit (EFP) application contains all the required information and warrants further consideration. The EFP would allow federally permitted fishing vessels to fish outside fishery regulations in support of exempted fishing activities proposed by the NOAA Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC). Regulations under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act require publication of this notification to provide interested parties the opportunity to comment on applications for proposed EFPs.

item.title: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: On October 30, 2025, DHS published an interim final rule (IFR) that amended DHS regulations to end the practice of automatically extending the validity of employment authorization documents (Forms I- 766 or EADs) for aliens who have timely filed an application to renew their EAD in certain employment authorization categories. This final rule responds to comments received on the IFR and reaffirms and finalizes the provisions of the IFR. Ending the automatic extension of EADs enhances benefit integrity and prioritizes the proper vetting and screening of aliens before granting a new period of employment authorization and/or a new EAD.

item.title: BNC Notice & Service Disruption — U.S. Bankruptcy Court, District of Maine — News & Announcements
item.description: Thursday, October 15, 2026 The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF. At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. Additionally, the following websites are unavailable: bnc.uscourts.gov bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov notices.uscourts.gov National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, October 15, 2026

The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors.

The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF.

At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. 

Additionally, the following websites are unavailable:

  • bnc.uscourts.gov
  • bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov
  • notices.uscourts.gov
  • National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels

The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.
